interest: This file provides a valuable window into the diplomatic maneuvering and economic intelligence operations in Southeast Asia and the Pacific during the tense summer of 1941, just months prior to the outbreak of the Pacific War. It illustrates how commercial and cultural exhibitions—specifically the 'Greater South Seas' Exhibition—were recognized by U.S. and Allied officials as calculated propaganda instruments designed to legitimize Japan's Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere and regional hegemony. The records highlight close behind-the-scenes alignment among the United States, Great Britain, the Netherlands East Indies, and the Philippine Commonwealth, while revealing the nuanced constitutional balance within the Philippines, where colonial authorities could steer government policy against participation but lacked legal power to ban private commercial exhibitors.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.607 South Seas, covering June to September 1941) details United States diplomatic and consular efforts to monitor and counter Japanese propaganda surrounding the proposed 'Greater South Seas' Exhibition (organized by the Union of South Sea Associations with Japanese Government backing) scheduled for October 1941 in Tokyo, Osaka, and Fukuoka. Following urgent warning telegrams from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo pointing out that the exhibition was intended to advance Japanese political and economic hegemony under the guise of the 'co-prosperity sphere,' the State Department instructed U.S. High Commissioner Francis B. Sayre to ensure the Philippine Commonwealth Government declined to participate. Simultaneously, Acting Secretary Sumner Welles issued confidential instructions to American consular posts across the region—including Batavia, Singapore, Rangoon, and Sydney—to discreetly investigate Japanese overtures, yielding reports that Dutch, British, and colonial authorities firmly rejected or barred participation.

subfiles.about: The Department of State instructs Consul General Foote in Batavia to discreetly investigate Japanese negotiations for Netherlands Indies participation in the Tokyo exhibition.
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles (for the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of State Sumner Welles instructs American Consul General Walter A. Foote in Batavia to discreetly investigate Japanese overtures to the Netherlands Indies regarding the upcoming Greater South Seas Exhibition in Tokyo. Foote is informed that the exhibition, sponsored by the Union of South Sea Associations with Japanese Government backing, promotes Japan's co-prosperity sphere. Welles notes that the U.S. High Commissioner to the Philippines has already been advised to discourage Philippine participation due to the exhibition's imperialistic objectives.
subfiles.title: Instruction from State Department to Consul General Foote (Batavia) on Greater South Seas Exhibition
subfiles.to: Walter A. Foote, American Consul General, Batavia

subfiles.about: The Department of State instructs Consul General Palmer in Sydney to discreetly ascertain Australian involvement in the planned Tokyo exhibition.
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles (for the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: The Department of State directs American Consul General Ely E. Palmer in Sydney to discreetly gather information from Australian authorities regarding negotiations for participation in the Greater South Seas Exhibition in Tokyo. The instruction highlights that the exhibition serves to promote Japan's co-prosperity sphere scheme in the southern Pacific. Palmer is also informed of the U.S. advice provided to the Philippine Commonwealth Government against participating.
subfiles.title: Instruction from State Department to Consul General Palmer (Sydney) on Greater South Seas Exhibition
subfiles.to: Ely E. Palmer, American Consul General, Sydney

subfiles.about: Department of State circular instruction alerting consular officers to the Greater South Seas Exhibition and outlining U.S. policy against participation.
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles (for the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: This copy of the Department's July 9 confidential instruction outlines plans by the Union of South Sea Associations to hold a Greater South Seas exhibition in Tokyo from October 15-25, 1941. The recipient is asked to discreetly determine whether Japanese authorities have approached regional governments to secure exhibits. It emphasizes that participation is undesirable because the project aims to place areas across the southern Pacific under Japanese political and economic hegemony.
subfiles.title: Instruction from State Department regarding the Greater South Seas Exhibition
subfiles.to: Addressed in text to Department of Commerce & Patterns, San Diego (Consular / Commercial Officer)

subfiles.about: The Department of State instructs Consul Brady in Rangoon to investigate reported Japanese negotiations regarding Burmese participation in the exhibition.
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles (for the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary Sumner Welles instructs American Consul Austin C. Brady in Rangoon to discreetly inquire whether colonial authorities in Burma have been approached to participate in the Greater South Seas exhibition. The instruction explains the promotional purpose behind the exhibition and notes that Japanese-mandated islands, French Indochina, and Thailand have already arranged participation. Brady is informed of the American Government's policy discouraging regional participation.
subfiles.title: Instruction from State Department to Consul Brady (Rangoon) on Greater South Seas Exhibition
subfiles.to: Austin C. Brady, American Consul, Rangoon

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports on plans by the Union of South Sea Associations to hold a government-backed Greater South Seas exhibition in Japan.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reports from Tokyo that the Union of South Sea Associations, representing sixteen affiliated groups, is organizing a Greater South Seas exhibition to promote Japan's co-prosperity sphere. The event is scheduled to take place in Tokyo from October 15 to 25, 1941, before traveling to Osaka and Fukuoka. Grew confirms that the Japanese Government is supporting the project and that participation has already been arranged for the Japanese Mandated Islands, French Indochina, and Thailand, with negotiations underway elsewhere.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 803 from Ambassador Grew (Tokyo) on Greater South Seas Exhibition
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, U.S. Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew questions the advisability of Philippine participation in the Greater South Seas Exhibition.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: In a follow-up to his previous telegram, Ambassador Grew advises Washington that, given the overt policy of the Union of South Sea Associations to advance the co-prosperity sphere program, he questions whether the Philippine Islands should participate in the exhibition. The message was received in confidential code and routed through key State Department divisions including Far Eastern Affairs and Philippine Affairs.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 804 from Ambassador Grew (Tokyo) recommending against Philippine participation
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, U.S. Secretary of State

subfiles.about: The State Department instructs High Commissioner Sayre to advise the Philippine Commonwealth Government against participating in the exhibition.
subfiles.summary: Repeating Ambassador Grew's report from Tokyo, the Department of State directs U.S. High Commissioner Francis B. Sayre in Manila to inform the Philippine Commonwealth Government that participation in the Tokyo exhibition would be undesirable. The Department emphasizes that the exhibition aims to advance Japan's co-prosperity sphere and place the southern Pacific, including the Philippines, under Japanese political and economic hegemony. Sayre is instructed to report back on the Commonwealth Government's response.
subfiles.title: State Department telegram instructing High Commissioner Sayre to dissuade Philippine participation
subfiles.to: American Consul, Manila (for U.S. High Commissioner Francis B. Sayre)

subfiles.about: The State Department informs Ambassador Grew that High Commissioner Sayre has been instructed to advise the Philippines against exhibition participation.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, U.S. Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: In response to Ambassador Grew's telegram No. 804, the Department of State confirms that action has been taken regarding the Philippines. The Department informs the Embassy in Tokyo that High Commissioner Sayre at Manila is being instructed to notify the Commonwealth Government that participation by the government or its agencies in the proposed South Seas exhibition is undesirable.
subfiles.title: State Department Telegram No. 333 to Embassy Tokyo regarding Philippine non-participation

subfiles.about: The State Department transmits Tokyo's report on the exhibition to High Commissioner Sayre via Naval Radio.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, U.S. Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull repeats Tokyo's telegram No. 803 to U.S. High Commissioner Sayre in Manila for his information via Naval Radio. The repeated text details the organization, dates, and locations of the exhibition, as well as the territories being lobbied to participate. This provided the documentary basis for Sayre's discussions with Philippine officials.
subfiles.title: State Department Telegram No. 239 transmitting Tokyo's report to High Commissioner Sayre

subfiles.about: Official paraphrase of telegram No. 238 instructing High Commissioner Sayre to discourage Philippine participation.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, U.S. Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: This confidential paraphrase records telegram No. 238 sent from Washington to High Commissioner Sayre in Manila. It instructs Sayre to acquaint the Philippine Commonwealth Government with Tokyo's report and explain the American Government's view that participation in the exhibition would be undesirable and contrary to Commonwealth interests. The paraphrase was also prepared for transmission to the Department of the Interior.
subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Telegram Sent No. 238 to High Commissioner Sayre

subfiles.about: Official paraphrase of telegram No. 239 repeating Tokyo's intelligence to High Commissioner Sayre.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, U.S. Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: This document provides the official paraphrase of telegram No. 239 sent to High Commissioner Sayre, conveying the full contents of Ambassador Grew's telegrams Nos. 803 and 804. It recounts the sponsorship of the Greater South Seas exhibition by the Union of South Sea Associations and Japanese Government backing. It concludes with Grew's assessment questioning the advisability of Philippine participation.
subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Telegram Sent No. 239 repeating Tokyo's report to High Commissioner Sayre

subfiles.about: High Commissioner Sayre reports that the Philippine Commonwealth Government will not participate in the exhibition.
subfiles.from: Francis B. Sayre, U.S. High Commissioner to the Philippines
subfiles.summary: High Commissioner Sayre reports from Manila that the Secretary to President Quezon has been verbally briefed on the contents of the Department's instructions. The Secretary assured Sayre that the Commonwealth Government has done nothing and will do nothing to participate in the exhibition, and will advise organizations like the Chamber of Commerce against participating. However, the Secretary noted that the Commonwealth could hardly prohibit private Philippine firms if they chose to exhibit independently.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 284 from High Commissioner Sayre on Philippine non-participation
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, U.S. Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Paraphrased record of High Commissioner Sayre's telegram reporting the Philippine Commonwealth's agreement not to participate.
subfiles.from: Francis B. Sayre, U.S. High Commissioner to the Philippines
subfiles.summary: This paraphrased record of telegram No. 284 documents High Commissioner Sayre's report on the Philippine Commonwealth's stance. It confirms verbal assurances from President Quezon's Secretary that the Commonwealth Government will abstain from the Tokyo exhibition and discourage local business organizations from participating. It also notes the Commonwealth's view that it could not strictly bar private commercial enterprises from exhibiting.
subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Telegram Received No. 284 from High Commissioner Sayre
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, U.S. Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Consul General Foote reports that the Netherlands Indies colonial government rejected Japan's exhibition invitation.
subfiles.from: Walter A. Foote, American Consul General, Batavia
subfiles.summary: Responding to the Department's confidential instruction of July 9, Consul General Walter A. Foote reports from Batavia regarding the Netherlands East Indies. He states that the colonial government was approached by Japan through the Netherlands Legation in Tokyo. The colonial administration rejected the invitation, formally replying that the present time was not appropriate for such an exhibition.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 84 from Consul General Foote (Batavia) on Dutch rejection of invitation
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, U.S. Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Consul Brady reports that Burma has received no Japanese invitation and would categorically reject participation.
subfiles.from: Austin C. Brady, American Consul, Rangoon
subfiles.summary: Consul Austin C. Brady acknowledges the Department's July 9 instruction regarding the Greater South Seas Exhibition and reports on his discussion with the Secretary of the Defence Department of the Government of Burma. The Secretary stated that while British authorities had alerted Burma telegraphically from London about the exhibition, no Japanese approach had been made. The Secretary emphatically rejected any possibility of Burmese participation, declaring, 'We would not think of such a thing.'
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 483 from Consul Brady (Rangoon) on Burma's refusal to participate
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, U.S. Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Consul General Patton reports that British authorities in Singapore received instructions from London barring participation in the exhibition.
subfiles.from: K. S. Patton, American Consul General, Singapore
subfiles.summary: Consul General K. S. Patton reports on his informal consultation with the Colonial Secretary of the Straits Settlements regarding the Greater South Seas Exhibition. The Colonial Secretary confidentially revealed that although no direct Japanese overture had occurred in Singapore, explicit instructions had been received from London barring any colonial participation. The Colonial Secretary presumed that the Japanese Government had approached British authorities directly in London.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1273 from Consul General Patton (Singapore) on British prohibition of participation
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, U.S. Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Archival docket cover sheet for Despatch No. 93 received from an American Consulate General concerning the exhibition.
subfiles.summary: This archival docket cover sheet records the receipt and administrative filing of Despatch No. 93 by the State Department's Division of Far Eastern Affairs on September 6, 1941. Originating from an American Consulate General (Consul General Palmer in Sydney, corresponding to the sequence of July 9 circular instructions), it was indexed under decimal file 894.607 SOUTH SEAS/6. The cover sheet marks the completion of diplomatic reporting on regional non-participation in the Tokyo exhibition.
subfiles.title: Cover sheet for Despatch No. 93 on the Greater South Seas Exhibition
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
